title: ARCH↔FW-001: HAL/RTOS Contracts & Resource Budgets + Firmware Conformance
description: The Embedded Systems Architect provides the HAL (Hardware Abstraction Layer) boundary definition, RTOS (Real-Time Operating System) selection, interface contracts, message schemas, OTA (Over-the-Air) strategy, and real-time / power / per-node resource budgets; the Firmware Engineer provides contract-conformant firmware, measured resource usage (Flash/SRAM, current, latency, jitter), feasibility flags on the proposed abstraction, and ADR proposals when a contract proves infeasible. Grounded in EMBEDDED_SYSTEMS_ARCHITECT_SKILL §6.3 and FIRMWARE_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.1. A budget exceedance or an infeasible contract is raised as an ADR (Never-Silently-Deviate); the ± tolerance bands of CLAUDE §6.5 are not yet instantiated, so a within_budget boolean is reported rather than a fabricated margin.

architecture_handoff.description: ARCH→FW: HAL boundary, RTOS, interface contracts, message schemas, OTA strategy, resource budgets, deadlines.

firmware_conformance.description: FW→ARCH: conformance verdict, measured usage, feasibility flags, infeasibility ADR.

exceedance_adr_ref.description: Required when within_budget = false (budget exceedance → ADR, not a silent trade).

infeasibility_adr_ref.description: Required when contract_conformant = false (infeasible contract → ADR proposal).

unit.description: Explicit unit, e.g., KB, mW, mA, ms, µs.

x-macp.tier_rationale: The architecture→firmware contract handoff (HAL/RTOS/budgets/message schemas/OTA strategy) crosses the architecture/implementation boundary and is ratified by humans. Budget exceedance or contract infeasibility is raised as an ADR (Tier-2 governance) — never silently traded; a breaking message-schema/contract change additionally requires a CCR + version bump.
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER (contract handoff at planning; conformance reviews during development; integration checkpoints; ADR consultation on any boundary/contract change)
confirm_conditions: every budget and measured-usage quantity (Flash/SRAM/power/current/latency/jitter) carries an explicit unit
the firmware conformance verdict is stated; measured resource usage is reported against the budgets
a budget exceedance carries a budget-exceedance ADR reference; an infeasible contract carries an infeasibility ADR reference
interface contracts and message schemas referenced are current and versioned
reject_conditions: a budget, timing, or current quantity emitted without a unit (units rule §3.10)
a measured budget exceedance presented as conformant without an ADR (Never-Silently-Deviate)
a ratified interface contract / message schema altered without a CCR + version bump
counter_conditions: a fabricated ± tolerance band invoked to call an over-budget measurement 'within budget' — CLAUDE §6.5 bands are NOT YET AVAILABLE; request the instantiated band or raise the ADR
a feasibility flag is ambiguous on whether the contract is implementable — request a measured infeasibility analysis before sign-off
